study.title: Peripheral ERK modulates acupuncture-induced brain neural activity and its functional connectivity

extraction_notes.note: This is an animal (mouse) study, not a human neuroimaging study. The 'neuroimaging' modality is c-Fos immunohistochemistry in mouse brain sections, not fMRI, PET, EEG, or MEG. All extracted neural data are histological c-Fos cell counts and derived network metrics, not standard neuroimaging signals.

Exact MNI or stereotaxic coordinates are not reported for any brain region. Brain region localization was based on The Mouse Brain in Stereotaxic Coordinates (Franklin & Paxinos 2008), not a human atlas. x/y/z fields are null throughout.
Sensory/interoceptive responses (deqi, pain sensation) were not measured or reported. This is an animal study; such responses are not applicable.
Expectancy, blinding credibility, and allocation guessing measures are not applicable to this animal study and were not reported.

Exact group sample sizes for brain immunohistochemistry are reported per brain region in Table 1 (varying n values per region), not as a single total. Total n per arm is not clearly stated for the brain study; values range from n=5 to n=10 per region depending on analysis.

Contrast task PLS salience score figures (Figure 4A, 4B) and functional connectivity circular layouts (Figure 5C) and force atlas formats (Figure 6A, 6B) contain results not available as tables. Specific statistical values from PLS are not numerically reported in text; only direction and dominant region are described.

Hot plate test results (Figure 1B) are presented as a bar graph (% of control) with mean ± SEM. Exact numeric values for each group are not given in text; only statistical comparison statements are provided.

Supplementary Table 1 (2-DE protein candidates) and Supplementary Figures 1A, 1B, 1C (p-ERK, p-HSP27, PRDX1 time courses) and Supplementary Figure S2 (full-length western blots) are referenced but not provided in the main PDF.

For the brain functional connectivity analysis, the exact group n per arm for the c-Fos quantification differs by brain region (as shown in Table 1). The authors do not report a single definitive n per arm for the network/connectivity analysis.

PH (posterior hypothalamic area) c-Fos values show ACU=27.6±0.3 n=8, which appears to be a very small SEM relative to the mean. This may reflect limited variability in that group but may also represent a potential OCR/typographical issue in the PDF. The value is transcribed as reported.

The paper reports F-statistics with different degrees of freedom for each brain region ANOVA (e.g., F2,20, F2,21, F2,22 etc.), reflecting different n values across regions. These have been preserved as reported in the corresponding row entries.

The ACU group c-Fos value for ARC is reported as 12.4±1.2 with P<0.001 vs CON (CON=10.5±1.1). The F statistic value F2,23=26.32 with P<0.001 is preserved as stated. The magnitude of change appears modest relative to the F-statistic, which is preserved as reported.

Network edge-level statistics (specific Pearson r values, exact betweenness centrality values per node) are not reported numerically in text or tables. Only relative rankings (above/below 80th percentile) and qualitative descriptions of high connectivity are provided.

The paper uses c-Fos IEG expression as a surrogate for 'neural activity' and inter-regional correlation of c-Fos counts as a surrogate for 'functional connectivity.' These are not standard fMRI-based functional connectivity measures. This distinction is important for any meta-analysis.

The arm_ACU_C (CPZ) and arm_ACU_D (DPCPX) groups were only used for the western blot protein expression experiments (peripheral ERK and p-HSP27), not for brain neural activity or functional connectivity analysis.
